ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, two chords intersect inside the circle, and the minor arc between the two endpoints on the circle on the left side is labeled 28°. The angle on the left side of the intersection inside the circle is labeled angle 3. There is also an inscribed angle labeled 12° in the figure, which is formed by chords connected to the two endpoints on the circle on the right side. Reasoning: Let the left endpoints of the two intersecting chords be A and B, and the right endpoints be C and D; angle 3 is the angle intercepted by the intersecting chords on the left side. From the figure, read the minor arc AB = 28°. The 12° inscribed angle intercepts the corresponding minor arc CD between the two endpoints on the right side, so arc CD = 2 × 12° = 24°. By the theorem of two chords intersecting inside a circle, the angle formed by intersecting chords equals half the sum of the measures of the two arcs intercepted by that angle and its vertical angle, therefore m∠3 = 1/2(28° + 24°) = 26°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $m\angle 3$. Assume that segments that appear tangent are tangent.

method.method_draft: Name the two chords that cross inside the circle so that angle 3 is the angle between their two left-side endpoints. Read from the diagram that the minor arc between those two left endpoints is labeled 28°. Also read the 12° inscribed angle formed by chords to the two right-side endpoints; this inscribed angle intercepts the opposite minor arc, so that arc measures 2·12° = 24°. Apply the intersecting-chords angle theorem: an angle formed by two chords intersecting inside a circle equals half the sum of the measures of the arcs intercepted by that angle and its vertical angle. Thus m∠3 = 1/2(28 + 24) = 26°.
